md_description: This DAG describes a rodent brain-slice electrophysiology workflow in which acute slices are prepared, exposed to pharmacological agents, and measured by patch-clamp recording to quantify synaptic responses. The pipeline produces processed electrophysiological features and a metadata table capturing neurotransmitter systems studied, causal receptor interactions, species and brain-region context, and supporting published references for the inferred plasticity findings.

rodent_brain_slice.reasoning: For the rodent_brain_slice Entity node, I included only intrinsic identity/origin/context fields that describe what the slice is before any drug exposure or recording: species, strain, age, sex, brain region, slice type, slice thickness, preparation freshness, and the ex vivo preparation status. I excluded pharmacology, recording settings, raw data properties, processed metrics, and literature annotations because those belong to downstream Process/Capture/Signal/Derivative nodes. I also avoided sample/experiment identifiers because root-level identifiers should not be repeated elsewhere. No already_generated fields were provided, so there were no direct collisions to avoid.

md_schema.descr: Rodent species used to prepare the acute brain slice, recorded at the entity level before any perfusion or recording; examples: Mus musculus, Rattus norvegicus.
Rodent strain or stock from which the slice was obtained, recorded at preparation time to capture biological background; examples: C57BL/6J, Sprague Dawley, Wistar.
Age of the animal at tissue collection, in postnatal days, measured once when the slice was prepared; typical range in acute slice studies is ~7-120 days depending on the preparation.
Biological sex of the donor animal used for slice preparation, recorded at the entity level because it is an intrinsic specimen attribute; examples: male, female, unknown.
Anatomical brain region from which the acute slice was prepared, recorded before any experimental manipulation; examples: hippocampus, cortex, striatum, amygdala, thalamus.

Type of ex vivo preparation represented by this entity, indicating that the tissue is an acute brain slice used for electrophysiology; this is fixed for this node and should not describe the recording method.
Thickness of the prepared brain slice in micrometers, measured during tissue preparation after slicing and before drug exposure or patch-clamp recording; typical range is about 150-500 µm.
Time elapsed in minutes between slice preparation and the start of downstream exposure/recording, used as a freshness proxy at the entity level; typical values are on the order of 10-240 minutes.
Status flag indicating that the specimen is an ex vivo acute preparation rather than in vivo tissue or culture; used to distinguish the biological material before any process steps.

pharmacological_perfusion.reasoning: For the pharmacological_perfusion Process node, I included only protocol and reagent-operation fields that describe how the bath application was performed: perfusion duration, vehicle, bath temperature, flow rate, drug names, target neurotransmitter system, target receptor, concentration, timing relative to recording, and whether washout was performed. I excluded slice identity fields (species, region, thickness), downstream recording/capture settings, raw signal properties, and analyzed plasticity outputs because those belong to the Entity, Capture, Signal, and Derivative nodes respectively. No already_generated fields were provided here, so there were no naming collisions to avoid.

md_schema.descr: Total time in minutes that the slice was exposed to bath-applied pharmacological agents during this process step; measured from onset of perfusion to termination or washout, typically ranging from minutes to hours.
Temperature of the perfusion bath in degrees Celsius during drug application, measured at the slice during the perfusion process; typical range is about 20-37 °C.
Bath perfusion flow rate in milliliters per minute applied during pharmacological exposure, recorded at the process step and typically in the range of ~1-10 mL/min depending on chamber setup.
Solvent or carrier used to deliver the pharmacological agents during bath application, recorded for the process to document baseline exposure conditions; examples: aCSF, DMSO, ethanol.

Names of the pharmacological agents bath-applied in this process step to modulate neurotransmitter release or receptor activity; use standardized drug names or common lab names, e.g. bicuculline, CNQX, APV.

Final bath concentration of the applied pharmacological agent in micromolar units, measured as part of the perfusion process; typical experimental range is nanomolar to millimolar depending on the compound.

Primary neurotransmitter system intended to be modulated by the perfused compound(s), recorded at the process level for experimental design; examples: glutamatergic, GABAergic, dopaminergic, cholinergic, serotonergic.
Specific receptor or receptor class targeted by the pharmacological agent during perfusion, captured at the process step; examples: AMPA receptor, NMDA receptor, GABA_A receptor, mGluR1.
When the pharmacological perfusion was applied relative to patch-clamp recording, recorded as a process attribute to support reproducibility; examples: preincubation, during_recording, both.
Whether the bath-applied pharmacological agent was washed out after exposure in this process step, documented to indicate reversibility testing or return to baseline conditions.
Duration in minutes of the washout phase following drug exposure, measured only if washout was performed; typical range is minutes to tens of minutes.

drug_treated_slice.reasoning: For the drug_treated_slice Entity node, I included only post-exposure specimen state fields that describe the slice as a biological object after pharmacological treatment and before capture: treatment status, exposure completion, last applied drug(s), residual drug presence, recovery time, and readiness for recording. I excluded any perfusion protocol parameters because those belong to the upstream Process node, and I excluded recording settings, raw data properties, and processed metrics because those belong to downstream Capture, Signal, and Derivative nodes. No already_generated fields were provided in this turn, so there were no collisions to avoid; I also avoided repeating intrinsic tissue identity fields already assigned to the root slice entity.

md_schema.descr: State of the slice after pharmacological exposure and before electrophysiological measurement; use this field to indicate that the specimen is drug-treated rather than untreated.
Whether the planned pharmacological exposure step was completed before the slice advanced to recording; recorded at the entity level immediately after perfusion and before capture.
Name or names of the final pharmacological agent(s) remaining associated with this slice after exposure, recorded at the post-treatment entity stage; examples: bicuculline, CNQX, APV.
Whether pharmacological agent is expected to remain in the slice/bath at the time it is handed off to recording, indicating incomplete washout or maintained drug condition.

Time in minutes between the end of drug exposure and the start of electrophysiological measurement, captured for the treated slice to document stabilization before recording; typical values range from 0 to tens of minutes.
Whether the treated slice meets criteria to proceed to patch-clamp measurement, such as intact tissue and stable exposure conditions, assessed immediately before the capture step.
Brief categorical description of the slice condition after pharmacological treatment and before recording; examples: equilibrated, washed, continuously_exposed.

patch_clamp_recording.reasoning: I corrected the capture-schema collision by removing bath_temperature_celsius, which had already been generated for a previous DAG step. I kept only capture-specific instrument and acquisition settings that remain unique to the patch-clamp session and do not duplicate upstream entity/process metadata or downstream signal/derivative fields. I also retained the capture-side description of chamber conditions via other non-colliding acquisition parameters, while avoiding any overlap with already generated fields.

md_schema.descr: Patch-clamp configuration used during the recording session, recorded at capture time; examples: whole_cell, voltage_clamp, current_clamp, cell_attached.

General recording setup used for the capture session, indicating whether the measurement was single-cell or multi-cell and whether one or more channels were acquired; examples: single_channel, dual_channel, multi_channel.
Manufacturer model name of the patch-clamp amplifier used during the recording session, recorded as part of the capture instrument description; example format: Axopatch 200B.
Serial number of the patch-clamp amplifier used in the capture session, recorded to identify the exact hardware unit; example format: SN123456.
Model name of the headstage/preamplifier attached to the amplifier during recording, captured as an instrument component used in this session; example format: HS-2A.
Analog-to-digital conversion sampling rate in kilohertz used during the patch-clamp capture session, measured as an acquisition setting; typical range is about 5-100 kHz depending on the protocol.
Low-pass filter cutoff in kilohertz applied during acquisition to the patch-clamp signal, recorded as an instrument setting at capture time; typical values are about 1-10 kHz.
Membrane holding potential in millivolts applied during the capture session, recorded as a configured recording parameter; typical range is approximately -90 to +40 mV depending on clamp mode.
Patch pipette resistance in megaohms measured/selected for the recording session before seal formation or whole-cell access; typical range is about 2-10 MΩ.

Artificial cerebrospinal fluid composition used in the recording chamber during patch-clamp capture, described by key ionic components and major additives; examples include NaCl, KCl, CaCl2, MgCl2, glucose, HEPES.
Junction potential correction in millivolts applied to the acquired recording session, recorded as a capture setting used to correct measured voltages; typical values are often 0-15 mV.
Duration in seconds of each recorded sweep or trial during the capture session, measured at acquisition time; typical values range from fractions of a second to several minutes.
Reference description for the electrical ground or reference electrode used during the patch-clamp capture, recorded to document the measurement setup; examples: bath_ground, Ag/AgCl_reference.

raw_synaptic_trace.reasoning: For the raw_synaptic_trace Signal node, I included only raw file/artefact descriptors: file format, file size, time and voltage/current dimensions, channel count, sweep count, storage location, recording duration in the file, and basic technical quality flags. I excluded capture settings such as bath temperature because that belongs to the upstream Capture node and was also already generated elsewhere in the DAG, and I excluded biological context, pharmacology, and computed feature fields because those belong to Entity/Process/Derivative nodes. I also ensured not to repeat any already_generated field names or semantically equivalent capture fields.

md_schema.descr: Digital file format of the raw synaptic trace artifact produced by the patch-clamp recording, recorded at the signal level; examples: ABF, DAT, CSV, NWB.

Size of the raw signal file in bytes, measured from the stored artifact after acquisition and before any downstream processing; typical values range from kilobytes to gigabytes depending on recording length.
Number of sampled time points in the raw trace file, describing the length of the signal axis in the stored artifact; measured from the file contents after acquisition.

Number of recording channels contained in the raw trace artifact, measured from the file structure after acquisition; examples include 1 for single-channel recordings or higher for multichannel acquisitions.
Number of individual sweeps or trials stored in the raw electrophysiology file, recorded from the artifact contents after acquisition and before analysis.

Sampling rate in hertz encoded in the raw trace file metadata, as stored in the signal artifact rather than as an acquisition setting; typical values are in the kilohertz-to-hundreds-of-kilohertz range.
Total duration in seconds of the raw trace represented in the file, measured from the stored artifact; use this as a signal-length descriptor rather than a capture-time setting.

File system path or object-store location where the raw synaptic trace is archived, recorded at the signal level for data retrieval; example format: /data/run01/raw_trace.abf or s3://bucket/path/file.abf.
Predominant polarity of the raw electrophysiological trace, indicating whether the stored artifact is voltage or current oriented; examples: voltage, current.
Basic technical quality assessment of the raw trace artifact after acquisition and before processing, such as whether the file is usable for downstream analysis.

electrophysiology_processing.reasoning: For the electrophysiology_processing Process node, I included only software/workflow parameters that describe how raw synaptic traces were transformed into analyzed features: pipeline name, software version, repository, algorithm family, baseline window, event detection threshold, smoothing, artifact rejection, normalization method, and output feature set. I excluded raw signal file properties because those belong to the upstream Signal node, and I excluded the computed metric values themselves because those belong to the downstream Derivative node. I also avoided repeating the previously generated bath_temperature_celsius field and any other capture-side settings.

md_schema.descr: Name of the electrophysiology analysis workflow used to process raw synaptic traces into features and plasticity metrics, recorded at the process step; example format: my_ephys_pipeline.
Version of the analysis software or pipeline used for electrophysiology processing, recorded to make the transformation reproducible; example format: 1.2.0.
Repository or code source for the processing workflow used on the raw traces, recorded at the process step; example format: github.com/org/repo or a local codebase identifier.

Core algorithm family used to detect events or compute plasticity features from the raw recording, captured as a process attribute; examples: threshold_detection, template_matching, deconvolution, peak_finding.
Time window in seconds used to estimate baseline activity before feature extraction, measured during the processing step; typical values are fractions of a second to tens of seconds.

Detection threshold expressed in standard deviations above or below baseline noise used during event calling or feature extraction, recorded as a processing parameter; typical values are about 2-8 SD.
Window length in seconds used to smooth or filter the raw trace prior to feature extraction, recorded at the process step; typical values are milliseconds to seconds.
Whether artifact rejection was applied during electrophysiology processing before computing downstream features; recorded as a process control flag.
Method used to normalize the processed electrophysiological features prior to output, captured at the process step; examples: none, baseline_normalization, z_score, percent_change.

Named set of electrophysiological features produced by the processing workflow, described here only as the output category of the process (not the values themselves); examples: synaptic_response_features, plasticity_metrics.

plasticity_metrics.reasoning: For the plasticity_metrics Derivative node, I included only computed-result fields that describe the analyzed outputs themselves: amplitude, paired-pulse ratio, plasticity index, normalized response change, response direction, response window, and quality/confidence metrics for the derived measurements. I excluded raw trace properties, capture settings, and process parameters because those belong to Signal, Capture, and Process nodes respectively. I also avoided bath_temperature_celsius and other previously generated fields, and did not repeat upstream biological context such as species or brain region. The fields here are specifically about the computed synaptic response metrics, not how they were acquired.

md_schema.descr: Computed synaptic response amplitude in picoamperes derived from the processed electrophysiology data, reported for the derivative output; typical values depend on cell type and protocol and may range from a few pA to thousands of pA.

Computed paired-pulse ratio derived from two successive synaptic responses in the processed data, measured as response 2 divided by response 1; typical values are dimensionless and often near 0.5-2.0.

Computed synaptic plasticity index summarizing the direction and magnitude of response change in the derivative output, typically a unitless ratio or normalized score; common forms include post/pre response ratio or percent change.
Percent change in synaptic response relative to baseline computed from the processed data, reported as a derivative metric; values can be negative or positive depending on depression or potentiation.
Direction of the inferred plasticity effect based on the computed metrics, recorded as the derivative interpretation of the result; examples: potentiation, depression, no_change.
Named time window or epoch over which the derivative metrics were aggregated, recorded to indicate the analyzed segment of the recording; examples: baseline, induction, post_induction, late_phase.

Confidence or support score for the computed derivative metrics, reported as a quality indicator for the result; typical values are 0-1 if normalized or 0-100 if percent-scaled, depending on the analysis workflow.
Number of synaptic events or response events contributing to the computed derivative metrics, reported as a count of analyzed observations in the output result.

Computed effect size summarizing the magnitude of the plasticity result in the derivative output, typically unitless and reported alongside the primary metrics; examples include Cohen's d or standardized mean difference.
Outcome of the statistical test associated with the derived plasticity metrics, reported as a derivative-level result summary; examples: significant, not_significant.

metadata_table_builder.reasoning: For the metadata_table_builder Process node, I included only curation/workflow fields that describe how the final dataset metadata table was assembled from analyzed results plus annotations: table schema version, curation tool/workflow name, annotation source, neurotransmitter-system tagging method, causal interaction labeling method, study inclusion criteria, literature reference resolution, and table validation status. I excluded any fields that belong to the upstream Derivative data values (plasticity metrics) or downstream final table contents (species, brain region, receptor labels, references themselves) because the process node should describe how the table was built, not repeat the table's contents. I also avoided repeating previously generated field names such as bath_temperature_celsius and any capture/process parameters already assigned elsewhere in the DAG.

md_schema.descr: Version identifier for the metadata table schema used during assembly of the dataset, recorded at the curation process step to support reproducibility; example format: v1.0.0.
Name of the curation or assembly workflow used to combine analyzed results with annotations and references into the metadata table; example format: metadata_table_builder.
Version of the metadata table assembly workflow or curation script used for this process step; example format: 0.4.2.
Primary source(s) used for neurotransmitter-system annotations and causal interaction labels during table assembly; examples: manual_curation, literature_mining, ontology_mapping, mixed.
Method used to assign neurotransmitter-system annotations during metadata table construction; examples: manual_labeling, ontology_based_mapping, keyword_matching, model_assisted_curation.
Method used to assign causal receptor or neurotransmitter interaction labels in the assembled table; examples: manual_review, rule_based_inference, literature_evidence_synthesis.

Brief description of the criteria used to decide which studies or records were included when building the metadata table, recorded at the assembly step; examples: rodent acute slice patch-clamp, receptor modulation studies, plasticity endpoints reported.
Method used to resolve and standardize published study references during table assembly; examples: doi_lookup, pubmed_query, manual_bibtex_entry, mixed.
Citation style or formatting convention applied to literature references in the assembled metadata table; examples: apa, vancouver, bibtex, doi_only.
Status indicating whether the assembled metadata table passed validation checks at the end of the curation process; examples: validated, needs_review, failed_checks.
Count of records or rows combined into the metadata table during this assembly step, recorded as a process output summary; typical values are non-negative integers.

experiment_metadata_table.reasoning: I corrected the final Derivative-node schema by removing fields that collided with earlier DAG steps: species and brain_region were already generated upstream at the root Entity level and must not be repeated in the final metadata table node. I retained only fields that truly describe the derivative artifact itself and its row-level annotations: table format, schema version, row/column counts, record identifier, neurotransmitter system, receptor interaction label, causality direction, plasticity finding summary, reference identifiers/citation, and evidence strength. I excluded process, capture, signal, and upstream entity details to keep the node within its derivative semantic territory and avoid further collisions with already_generated fields.

md_schema.descr: Format of the final experiment metadata table artifact, recorded for the derivative output; examples: csv, tsv, parquet, json.
Version of the metadata schema used by the final table, recorded with the derivative artifact to support interpretation and reuse; example format: v1.0.0.
Number of records contained in the final experiment metadata table, measured from the derivative output artifact after assembly.
Number of columns present in the final experiment metadata table, measured from the derivative output artifact after assembly.

Unique string identifier for each row in the final metadata table; example format: exp_0001 or record_17. This identifier should be table-specific and not repeat sample or experiment identifiers from the root entity.
Neurotransmitter system annotated in the final table for each record, summarizing the signaling system investigated; examples: glutamatergic, GABAergic, dopaminergic, cholinergic, serotonergic.

Annotated receptor interaction label stored in the final metadata table, capturing the specific receptor or receptor class implicated by the study; examples: AMPA receptor, NMDA receptor, GABA_A receptor, mGluR1.

Direction of the inferred causal relationship stored in the final table, describing whether the receptor manipulation increased, decreased, or did not change the synaptic outcome; examples: positive, negative, null.

Concise summary of the synaptic plasticity result represented in the final metadata table, such as potentiation, depression, or no detectable change; this is a table-content field rather than a process or signal value.
Digital Object Identifier associated with the supporting published study referenced in the final metadata table; example format: 10.1038/s41586-020-XXXX-X.
Human-readable citation for the supporting published study as stored in the final metadata table; example formats may follow APA, Vancouver, or a journal-specific style.
Qualitative strength of evidence supporting the annotated causal interaction in the final table, recorded as a derivative-level summary; examples: strong, moderate, weak.
